status.en: 145 armed incidents reported in the past seven days, 18% fewer than the week before, most of them in Islamabad, Kabul and Balochistan.
status.nb: 145 væpnede hendelser meldt de siste sju dagene, 18 prosent færre enn uken før, flest i Islamabad, Kabul og Belutsjistan.

summary.en: Pakistan is confronting renewed cross-border tension as it blames Taliban fighters in Afghanistan for attacks while the Taliban rejects the claims and reports a surge in arrests after a Panjshir blast. The EU has launched a €5 million border-security project in Pakistan and is discussing labour mobility, while Pakistan has tested an extended-range Fatah‑2 hypersonic ballistic missile. Simultaneously, large caches of weapons and explosives have been seized near the India-Pakistan border in Rajasthan, and Pakistan has reaffirmed its defence commitment to Saudi Arabia amid Houthi attacks. The conflict produced 1,794 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Pakistan konfronterer fornyet grensekonflikt når landet legger skylden på Taliban-krigere i Afghanistan for angrep, mens Taliban avviser påstandene og melder om en økning i arrestasjoner etter en eksplosjon i Panjshir. EU har igangsatt et grensesikkerhetsprosjekt på 5 millioner euro i Pakistan og diskuterer arbeidsmobilitet, mens Pakistan har testet en langdistanse-Fatah‑2 hypersonisk ballistisk missil. Samtidig er store våpen- og sprengstofflagre blitt beslaglagt nær India-Pakistan-grensen i Rajasthan, og Pakistan har bekreftet sitt forsvarsløfte til Saudi-Arabia etter houthi-angrep. Konflikten førte til 1 794 dødsfall i kamper i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Insurgency in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa
background.extract: Since 2004, an insurgency has been fought in the Pakistani province of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa by Islamist militant groups such as the Tehrik-i-Taliban Pakistan (TTP), Jundallah, Lashkar-e-Islam (LeI), the Tehreek-e-Nafaz-e-Shariat-e-Mohammadi (TNSM), Al-Qaeda, and their Central Asian allies such as the Islamic State – Khorasan Province (ISKP), Islamic Movement of Uzbekistan, East Turkistan Movement, Jamaat-ul-Ahrar, Ittihad-ul-Mujahideen Pakistan, and elements of organised crime. Before being transformed into an insurgency in 2017, the conflict was a war.
